objective: Configuring and troubleshooting Windows Update, backup, and system restore
secondaryObjectives: Windows administrative tools: Task Manager, Disk Management, Control Panel, Settings app, and MMC snap-ins

sources.cite: CompTIA A+ Core 2 (220-1202) V15 Exam Objectives, Document Version 4.0: domains Operating systems 28%, Security 28%, Software troubleshooting 23%, Operational procedures 21%; launched 2025-03-25
sources.note: Objective 2.6 'Given a scenario, implement procedures for basic small office/home office (SOHO) malware removal', read in primary text in the objectives PDF on 2026-11-14: '1. Investigate and verify malware symptoms. 2. Quarantine infected system. 3. Disable System Restore in Windows Home. 4. Remediate infected systems. 5. Update anti-malware software. 6. Scan and removal techniques (e.g., safe mode, preinstallation environment) 7. Reimage/reinstall. 8. Schedule scans and run updates. 9. Enable System Restore and create a restore point in Windows Home. 10. Educate the end user.' Objective 3.4 lists 'False alerts regarding antivirus protection', 'Random/frequent pop-ups' and 'Redirection'. The exam page (summarizing fetch, same day) gives the domains and launch date. Reused for REQ-336 from this course's home-office-laptop-malware (the same reading and date); the objective wording is the course seed's.

The business, the users, the devices and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You are the desktop support technician at Hollins and Grey, a fictional accounting firm in tax season. Three tickets wait: an update that keeps failing, a PC that blue-screens after a printer driver install, and a partner asking whether backups work.
handover: PC ACC-07: a cumulative update fails at 35% and rolls back every night.
PC ACC-12: System Restore is on; a restore point was made before yesterday's driver install.
howItWorks: The desk shows the ticket queue against the priority matrix and each service's status.
Move on a ticket round at a time. A decision comes to you at each ticket round; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

wuPrompt.title: An update that keeps rolling back
wuPrompt.context: The update includes a security fix being exploited in the wild.

choices.label: Free space with Disk Cleanup (including old installer files), repair the component store with DISM and sfc, then install the update

effects.log: The update installs after the repair.

choices.feedback: The log named the causes: space and a corrupted store. Fix them, then update.

choices.label: Run Windows Update again tonight
choices.feedback: Nothing changed, so it fails the same way.

choices.label: Pause updates on ACC-07 for 35 days until tax season ends
choices.feedback: The exploited vulnerability stays open for a month on a PC holding client tax data.

restorePrompt.title: ACC-12 won't boot
restorePrompt.context: A restore point exists from before the driver install.

choices.label: Boot to the Windows Recovery Environment and use System Restore to the pre-driver restore point, then install the vendor's current driver

effects.log: Restored to before the driver; ACC-12 boots.

choices.feedback: System Restore rolls back drivers and system settings without touching user files.

choices.label: Boot to Safe Mode and remove the driver by hand

effects.log: The driver is removed in Safe Mode.

choices.feedback: It works, but takes longer and may leave pieces of the driver behind.

choices.label: Reset this PC, removing everything
choices.feedback: Reset removes the user's local files and apps; the partner's unsynced working papers are gone.

bkPrompt.title: Backups never tested
bkPrompt.context: Backups report success; the NAS share is writable from every PC.

choices.label: Restore a sample of files to a test folder to prove the backups work, remove the PCs' write access to the backup share, and add an offsite copy

effects.log: A test restore succeeds; the backup is no longer writable from PCs; offsite added.

choices.feedback: A backup is only proven by a restore; a backup any PC can write to can be encrypted by ransomware.

choices.label: Tell the partner the reports show success

effects.log: The partner is told they work.

choices.feedback: Success reports don't prove you can restore.

choices.label: Delete old backup versions to save NAS space
choices.feedback: Without old versions, a file corrupted last month can't be recovered.

scoring.modelReasoning: When Windows Update fails, read the update history and Event Viewer: low disk space and a corrupted component store are fixed with Disk Cleanup, DISM and sfc. A driver that breaks boot is undone with System Restore from the recovery environment, which keeps user files; reset removes them. A backup is proven only by a test restore, keeps versions, and needs a copy ransomware on a PC can't reach.
